M

How this was measured

So you can re-run it, or disbelieve it on the evidence rather than on trust.

Targethttps://iris.akeyo.io only. No localhost, no local http.server, no mock. Before anything else, the local sources were compared against the live ones: index.html, js/app.js, js/registry.js, sw.min.js and verified_sources.md are byte-identical (sha1) to what the CDN serves — so reading the local code is reading the deployed code.
BrowserGoogle Chrome via puppeteer-core, headless: 'new', --mute-audio --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required, and a HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play patch that force-mutes every element.
Network captureFour independent channels per run so nothing hides: puppeteer's request/requestfailed/response hooks, an in-page fetch+XMLHttpRequest mirror installed before any app code runs, and — for the torrent and whisper rows — a CDP Network.requestWillBeSent feed that also catches service-worker- and worker-initiated requests.
TimingEvery millisecond figure names its two clock boundaries in the raw JSON. Where the number is a browser-internal one (paint, navigation) it comes from performance.getEntriesByType('navigation') inside the page, not from the harness's wall clock.
RepetitionPlayback rows were run 2–5 times in fresh browsers; medians are stated alongside every individual run, never instead of them.
Artifacts27 result JSONs and 53 screenshots under test/iris-live/ (results/ and shots/), each written by the script that measured it.
Which build this describesThe bytes GitHub Pages served between roughly 02:44 and 03:00 on 2026-08-23. Re-checked afterwards: index.html, js/app.js, sw.min.js and verified_sources.md are still byte-identical live. One exception: a parallel session has since edited js/player.js locally (a local-engine ffmpeg/HLS transcode path, ~25 lines) that is not deployed — the live file still hashes to the version measured here. That work was left untouched; nothing in this pass modified app source, .deploy/, or git.

The one thing that looks like an error and is not. Chrome reports a steady drip of https://iris.akeyo.io/?_n=<n> requests as net::ERR_ABORTED — 20 of them in the 20-second window. These are not the registry poller. They come from js/netmon.js:54, fetch(location.pathname + '?_n=' + t0, {method:'HEAD', cache:'no-store'}) on a setInterval(ping, 1500) — the live RTT gauge in the top bar. Chrome aborts a HEAD whose static host answers with a body; the app .catch()es it at netmon.js:56 and merely nulls the readout. The registry poller is separate and healthy: registry.js:111 fetches verified_sources.md every 2.5 s and every one of the 12 polls in the window returned 200.

Big Buck Bunny MP4 tile → playing

Click the Big Buck Bunny MP4 tile → the video element reaches playing / currentTime > 0. Measure click→first-frame.

PASS
PASS, by a genuine real-mouse-click measurement. Five fresh browsers, five real clicks on the tile, five full-player opens: click → first decoded frame 645 / 781 / 812 / 825 / 828 ms — median 812 ms, 0 failures. The catch is geometric: the tile's centre is unclickable, because the trust dock sits on top of it. Click the upper third of the same tile and it plays every time.
Clockt0 = page.mouse.click dispatched on CANVAS#wall · t1 = first 50 ms poll where a <video> inside .plr-root has currentTime > 0.15 && videoWidth > 0 && !paused
Click → first frame (real click, strict player)825 / 645 / 781 / 812 / 828 ms — min 645, median 812, max 828. 5/5 succeeded, 0 failures, 0 crashes.
What the click opensthe full-screen Player overlay directly — .plr-root appears at t+460…651 ms, Player.isOpen() === true, isInline() === false. No detail overlay, location.hash stays empty: registry rows bypass the detail route via onWallSelect → playRegistry → Player.play.
Same thing via the API412 / 458 ms (median 435 ms) calling Player.play() directly, and 471 / 461 ms from a third lane — consistent, and faster than the click path because it skips the wall's camera fly-to.
Video at first frame1280×720 · readyState 4 · duration 10.00 s · not paused · error null · parent class plr-root plr-in
SourcecurrentSrc = https://test-videos.co.uk/vids/bigbuckbunny/mp4/h264/720/Big_Buck_Bunny_720_10s_5MB.mp4 — straight from the CDN, no proxy, no blob
Playback heldcurrentTime advanced 3.005–3.015 s over 3 s in all five runs — real decode, not a frozen poster
Networkexactly one request to test-videos.co.uk per run, status 206, 0 failed. 0 requests to 127.0.0.1 / localhost / [::1] across all five runs. 0 pageerrors, 0 console errors.
The click that goes nowhere — root cause, measured. Five consecutive naive centre clicks on the Big Buck Bunny tile produced nothing: no player, no video element, no canvas event, in 5/5 runs over 45 s each. The reason is geometric, not logical. At 1440×900 the tile's rect is {left: 101.5, top: 717.7, w: 143.0, h: 214.6}, so its centre is (173, 825) — and document.elementFromPoint(173, 825) returns BUTTON#td-toggle.td-toggle, the bottom-left "honest ledger" trust dock, whose rect is {l: 15, t: 797, w: 377.2, h: 34}. Canvas listeners recorded 0 pointerdown, pointerup and click events; the trust dock opened instead (class="trustdock open") and 0 requests went to test-videos.co.uk. Exactly 1 of 7 registry tile centres is occluded at this viewport — a small, real UX hazard, not a playback defect.

Two independent controls pin it on the overlay rather than on the click handling. First: clicking (173, 771) — the same tile, upper third, where elementFromPoint returns CANVAS#wall — plays every single time. Second: the identical single-click gesture on the torrent tile at (708, 833) opens the player too. Same code, different pixels.

A trap this harness fell into, recorded so nobody repeats it. The wall shows a muted inline hover-preview of the same MP4, and in runs 4 and 5 that preview reached playing state at t+482 ms and t+509 ms — before .plr-root even existed (632 / 651 ms). A probe helper that falls back from .plr-root video to document.querySelector('video') will happily time the preview and report a flatteringly small number. The 812 ms median above is strict-player-only: every probe asserted Player.isOpen() and DOM ancestry inside .plr-root (unmuted, isInline() === false) rather than trusting the selector. The preview elements live in .plr-pv-wrap.plr-pv-in.plr-pv-playing and are always muted.

The first attempt at this row was wrong, and that matters. An earlier lane clicked the tile twice, found a <video> whose currentSrc was the raw magnet: URL with error.code === 4 and net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME, and recorded FAIL. That element was never the player — Player.isOpen() was false and BT.tryPlay had never been called. The probe helper falls back from .plr-root video to document.querySelector('video'), and picked up an inline wall preview instead. The row was re-run with an explicit Player.isOpen() assertion and full instrumentation, which is where the numbers above come from. The original FAIL is left in the record rather than deleted.

Whisper — vendored model, no CDN, and what auto-sync really does

Trigger the whisper engine load → model loads from /vendor without CDN (no huggingface.co / cdn). Report load ms. If it only loads on autosync, drive a minimal autosync and report honestly.

PARTIAL
The model half is a clean PASS; the auto-sync half is an honest PARTIAL. whisper-tiny.en_timestamped loads 38.26 MB entirely from iris.akeyo.io/vendor in 27,473 ms cold with 0 CDN requests across 129 URLs, and it really transcribes: 176 words out of live remote audio. What it cannot do on this deploy is produce a confident subtitle offset — and the reason is not the model.
Model loadWhisperTiny.enable() = 27,473 ms in-page (cold cache). Warm-cache repeats in other lanes: 3,173 ms, 3,862 ms, 4,799 ms.
Self-verifyWhisperTiny.verify() = 1,870 ms, returned {ok: true, words: 1} on 1 s of silence
CDN requests0. Regex /huggingface\.co|hf\.co|cdn\.jsdelivr|unpkg\.com|cdnjs/i over 129 URLs collected from puppeteer requests + failures + the in-page fetch/XHR mirror + a CDP Network.requestWillBeSent feed.
Why there is no CDN fallbackjs/whisper-tiny.js:55-62 sets env.allowLocalModels = true, env.allowRemoteModels = false, env.localModelPath = '/vendor/', wasm.wasmPaths = '/vendor/transformers/'. The vendored transformers.js still carries the huggingface.co and jsdelivr defaults, but allowRemoteModels:false and the explicit wasmPaths defuse both.
Bytes pulled from /vendor38.26 MB encoded (31.88 MB of it ONNX) — decoder q8 30,729,881 B + encoder fp16 16,477,869 B uncompressed
Deploy completeness (HTTP lane)all 25 files under vendor/ return 200 with byte-identical content-length; sha256 verified on the 4 heaviest; negative control /vendor/transformers/DOES_NOT_EXIST.wasm → 404, so no catch-all is faking those 200s
Backenddevice is hardcoded wasm. crossOriginIsolated === false on GitHub Pages (no COOP/COEP headers, which Pages cannot set), so no SharedArrayBuffer and ORT runs single-threaded — slower, still correct. navigator.gpu is present but unused.
It really transcribes (CORS-open source)on https://webtorrent.io/torrents/Sintel/Sintel.mp4 the app's own window cutter pulled 5 audio windows / 5,634,800 B over HTTP Range (206s) and whisper returned 176 words in 10 calls / 35,016 ms, windowMisses: 0. Verbatim sample: "Shh, shh, shh, … Hey, sit still." with word timestamps 205.30 → 215.98 s.
It also feeds on HLSon the Mux stream the TS window provider demuxed 1,292 AAC frames (44.1 kHz stereo) → 30 s decoded at 48 kHz → whisper windows 3 · windowMisses 1 · calls 4 · words 6 · 650,882 B · source "hls"
What did NOT happenno confident sync. SubsAutoSync.sync() reached phase "coherent" with coherent: false, score: 0, offset: 0 on both sources.
Why auto-sync cannot win on this deploy — two separate reasons, both measured.

(1) The MP4 demo rows are CORS-blocked for audio. On Big Buck Bunny the pipeline reported windows: 3, windowMisses: 3, calls: 0 — whisper was never even invoked. Proven from inside the live page: fetch(BBB, {headers:{Range:…}}) rejects with TypeError: Failed to fetch and Chrome logs "blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present". A bare GET is blocked too, so the Range header is not the trigger — test-videos.co.uk and media.w3.org simply send no ACAO at all. Ordinary playback still works because a plain <video src> is a no-CORS media load; the audio-window cutter at js/subs-audio-source.js:83 is a page-origin fetch() and must be refused. Same cutter, same version, on the ACAO-* webtorrent.io URL returns a real 1,166,351-byte AAC window. The cutter is not broken; four of the seven seed hosts are simply not CORS-open.

(2) On the CORS-open sources, the content does not match the subtitles. The only IMDb id with subtitles in this catalogue is tt10872600, whose 2,189 cues belong to a different film than the Mux and Sintel test streams. The coherence scorer looked for anchor phrases ("we come to you now with revelations") in the transcribed audio, found nothing, scored 0 and refused to apply an offset. That is the gate working correctly — a wrong offset would be worse than none.

So the honest verdict for row 6 is: the engine is real, vendored, CDN-free and produces correct word timestamps from live remote audio on the public site; end-to-end auto-sync is NOT VERIFIED on this deploy, because no seed row pairs CORS-open audio with a matching subtitle track. That is a catalogue property, not a code failure — and it is fixable by pointing the demo rows at ACAO-* mirrors.

Secondary defect worth fixing. Four nested ['catch'] handlers between subs-audio-source.js and whisper-engine.js:323 swallow the network failure, so the app reported phase: "coherent" in 72 ms with score: 0 and logged nothing. A hard, diagnosable CORS error was turned into a silent shrug. Surfacing the miss would have made this row a five-minute investigation instead of an hour.

Service worker registered — and its scope

Service worker registered (sw.min.js) — report scope.

PASS
PASS — and it is lazy by design, which is the interesting part. On a plain page load navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() is empty. After a real ▶ on the torrent tile the registration appears at 2,085 ms and reaches activated at 2,395 ms, scope https://iris.akeyo.io/.
Registrationjs/torrent.js:34 SW_URL = '/sw.min.js', registered at js/torrent.js:93 as navigator.serviceWorker.register(SW_URL, {scope: '/'}) inside ensureServer()
Triggerlazy — ensureServer() is reached only from BT.streamTo() (js/torrent.js:124), which player.js:1310 calls after BT.tryPlay() resolves. Nothing registers on a plain page load.
Scopehttps://iris.akeyo.io/ — root. No Service-Worker-Allowed header is needed because the script is served from the root itself.
Timing after a real ▶ clickregistration visible 2,085 ms · activated 2,395 ms · controls the page. A second lane saw installed → activating → activated all land at 5,245 ms from play.
ControllerscriptURL https://iris.akeyo.io/sw.min.js, state activated
The asset/sw.min.js → 200, 1,297 B, application/javascript; charset=utf-8, byte-identical to vendor/webtorrent-sw.min.js
What it actually doesinstall → skipWaiting(), activate → clients.claim(), and a fetch handler that intercepts only URLs containing scope + "webtorrent/". Everything else passes through untouched — no app-shell caching, no offline mode, no interception of site assets. It postMessages the request to the page and streams the torrent file back. The page is the origin server; the SW is the plumbing.
Observed in use/webtorrent/cancel/ and /webtorrent/08ada5a7…/Sintel/Sintel.mp4 — the second one is what the <video> played from
Note/sw.min.js.map → 404 (a dangling sourceMappingURL). DevTools-only, harmless.

Localhost resolver/engine calls fail gracefully

Resolver/engine localhost calls: confirm they fail gracefully (gated), no UI breakage.

PASS
PASS, better than the bar. On a plain load the page makes zero requests to 127.0.0.1 — both probes are lazy. When forced, they fail in 5 ms and 3 ms, and the app is completely unharmed: 0 new pageerrors, wall unchanged, and an MP4 still plays afterwards in 471 ms.
Unprompted requests to 127.0.0.10 on a plain page load — the probes are lazy, not fire-on-boot
<code>HP.resolverUp()</code>js/app.js:678-685 → fetchJSONT("http://127.0.0.1:11471/health", 800), AbortController at 800 ms. Measured: 5 ms / 4 ms → resolves false.
<code>Player.engineUp()</code>js/player.js:498-509 → fetchT("http://127.0.0.1:11470/status", 1000, {cache:'no-store'}). Measured: 1 ms / 3 ms → resolves false.
Why so fastChrome refuses before the socket: "Access to fetch at 'http://127.0.0.1:11471/health' from origin 'https://iris.akeyo.io' has been blocked by CORS policy: Permission was denied for this request to access the loopback address space." — Private Network Access, so the 800/1000 ms timeouts never even get a chance to fire.
Engine path is double-gatedjs/player.js:1379-1387 routeTorrentEngine() reaches engineUp() only when localStorage['hp.torrent.localEngine'] === '1'. By default the app shows the honest copy-magnet panel and never touches 127.0.0.1 at all.
UI after both probes failuncaught pageerrors before → after: 0 → 0 · HP.wallList().length unchanged · #gate still hidden · no blocking overlay · no error toast
Recovery checka normal MP4 played immediately afterwards — first frame in 471 ms and 461 ms across two runs
+

Beyond the eight rows

Things worth knowing that nobody asked for.

Cold vs warm. Cold load: loadEventEnd 414 ms, FCP 340 ms, 196,738 B transferred. Warm reload: 91.5 ms and 3.6 KB — a 98% byte reduction, courtesy of cache-control: max-age=600 on every Pages asset.
Five-minute soak. Left open for 307 seconds, sampled every 15 s: 0 uncaught pageerrors, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests other than the netmon RTT pings, 0 responses ≥ 400. HP.wallList().length held at 247, the render loop stayed running, DOM node count was constant at 335, and the JS heap went 5.02 MB → 4.75 MB (it collects; no leak signal over this window — 5 minutes is too short to prove absence, and that is stated as a limit, not a result). The app was still responsive to a real click at the end.
Mobile, 390×844 @3x, iPhone UA. The wall renders all 247 items, there is zero horizontal overflow (scrollWidth === innerWidth), and a tap plays video. One cosmetic bug: the #hp-net RTT gauge paints over the search field and the Home link.
The live-watch loop is capped on Pages. js/registry.js re-fetches verified_sources.md every 2.5 s with cache: 'no-store', and every poll returned 200. But the file is served with cache-control: max-age=600 behind Fastly, and repeated requests — even with a cache-busting query string — came back x-cache: HIT with age: 362, 363, 363. So an edit to the registry cannot appear on the public site faster than the edge TTL. The 3-second live-watch is a local-development property; on iris.akeyo.io it is up to ten minutes. Nothing is broken — but the claim needs its qualifier.
Four of seven seed rows are not CORS-open. test-videos.co.uk (3 rows) and media.w3.org (1 row) send no access-control-allow-origin header at all; an OPTIONS preflight to test-videos.co.uk returns 405. They play fine (a plain <video src> needs no CORS, and js/player.js:1405-1418 deliberately leaves crossOrigin off for exactly that reason) but no JS on the page can read their bytes — which is what costs row 6 its auto-sync. The Mux HLS rows and the webseeded torrent row are ACAO: * throughout, master playlist to .ts segment.
Chaturbate remains impossible client-side, as documented. POST https://chaturbate.com/get_edge_hls_url_ajax/ returns 200 with a JSON body and zero access-control-allow-* headers; the OPTIONS preflight returns 403. UNKNOWNS.md's claim is confirmed exactly — that hop needs a server, and the public deploy honestly does not pretend otherwise.
Deploy hygiene. HTTP/2, server: GitHub.com, /CNAME = 200 / 14 B / iris.akeyo.io, /.nojekyll = 200 / 0 B, /reports/index.html = 200. All 16 js/*.js files byte-identical to the repo. Grepping the downloaded JS for http:// finds exactly two hits — app.js:34 and player.js:10, both the gated loopback URLs — plus one xmlns inside a data: favicon. No mixed-content risk, no CDN dependency. No COOP/COEP (Pages cannot set them), which costs whisper its wasm threads and nothing else.
!

What is actually wrong

Four real findings, ranked. None of them stops the site working.

FindingImpactWhere
1 Auto-sync cannot complete on any seed row. Four rows are CORS-blocked for audio; the rest have no matching subtitle track. The engine works — the catalogue does not pair with it. feature dark catalogue + verified_sources.md
2 Failures are swallowed silently. Four nested ['catch'] handlers turn a hard CORS rejection into phase: "coherent", score: 0 in 72 ms with nothing logged. undiagnosable subs-audio-source.js:83/92 → whisper-engine.js:323
3 Hovering the torrent tile spawns a dead preview that spins forever. The registry hpUrl fast path feeds a raw magnet: straight into a pooled <video>.src. Reproduced twice on the live site; one-line fix identified. visible bug app.js:760 → player.js:2439
4 The trust dock eats clicks on the tile beneath it. At 1440×900 exactly one of seven registry tile centres resolves to BUTTON#td-toggle instead of the canvas. UX hazard #trustdock vs #wall
5 Cosmetic overlap on mobile — the #hp-net RTT gauge paints over the search field and the Home link at 390 px. cosmetic js/netmon.js / style.css
Finding 3 in full, because it is the only one a normal visitor will actually see. Hover the "Sintel (torrent — no server)" tile — no click needed — and the app builds a pooled preview element whose src is the raw magnet URL. Measured state: error.code 4, networkState 3 (NETWORK_NO_SOURCE), 0×0, one net::ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME per hover. Because the wrapper never receives the plr-pv-playing class, the CSS rule that hides the spinner never applies, so a 26 px loading spinner spins forever over the poster in a 356×533 overlay. It is also sticky: previewHas(key) stays true, so re-hovering takes the "instant resume" branch, never re-resolves, and re-marks the dead entry as the youngest in the pool — squatting 1 of 6 preview slots for the rest of the session.

The app already states the rule one screen above, at js/app.js:719-722: isDirectUrl() excludes magnets and the comment says "torrents need the engine + peers and are never previewed". But that filter lives only in pickPreviewable() on the addon branch; the registry hpUrl fast path at js/app.js:760 returns before ever reaching it. The main play path is guarded — player.js resolve() classifies magnets as kind torrent. One branch, one missing guard, and startPreviewFor() already handles a null result at js/app.js:861, so the fix is a single early return reusing predicates that already exist.

Nothing here was fixed. This was a verification pass, and the app source was read-only throughout — no file under index.html, js/, vendor/ or .deploy/ was modified, and no git command was run.

What this report does not prove

The honest boundary of the evidence.

End-to-end auto-syncNOT VERIFIED. Whisper transcribes and the pipeline runs, but no seed row pairs CORS-open audio with a matching subtitle track, so no correct offset was ever produced or could be.
WebRTC peer-to-peerNOT VERIFIED. Every torrent byte came from the HTTPS webseed (webSeeds: 1, webrtcPeers: 0). Two wss trackers were dead during the run (tracker.fastcast.nz unresolvable, tracker.btorrent.xyz refused). Browser-to-browser transfer was not observed and is not claimed.
Live-watch on the public hostThe 2.5 s poll works; the ≤3 s visible update does not survive a 600 s edge cache. Not tested by actually editing the deployed file.
Other browsersChrome only. Safari and Firefox were not tested — MSE, PNA loopback blocking and wasm behaviour all differ there.
Real devicesMobile was an emulated viewport + UA, not hardware.
Leak-freedomFive minutes of stable heap is a smoke test, not a proof.
The whisper speed claimThe in-source note "RTF ~0.16 on WASM" was not reproduced here. Measured on this deploy: 35,016 ms of engine time for 5 windows, single-threaded, with crossOriginIsolated === false.
